bug.description: The introduced guard `!suspense.isInFallback` inside the parent‑suspense check reverses the intended condition, causing root replacements to be applied even when a nested Suspense boundary is showing its fallback, which leads to mounting new content into a retained page.

fixPr.title: fix(suspense): skip a root replacement in a retained nested boundary showing its fallback (#16125)

pr.title: perf(hydration): avoid observer if element is in viewport (#11639)

bug.description: The new hydrationOnVisible strategy calls hydrate() and disconnects the observer as soon as any root element is visible, but it never observes children of elements with `display: contents`. This means nested visible elements are never observed, causing the observer to stay active and hydration to miss visible children.

fixPr.title: fix(hydration): observe children of a display: contents root in hydrateOnVisible (#15773)

diff --git a/packages/vitest/src/node/reporters/renderers/trace-timeline.ts b/packages/vitest/src/node/reporters/renderers/trace-timeline.ts
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..a8680b9b8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/vitest/src/node/reporters/renderers/trace-timeline.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,207 @@
+import type { TestArtifact } from '../../../runtime/runner/types'
+import { relative } from 'pathe'
+import c from 'tinyrainbow'
+import { F_TREE_NODE_END, F_TREE_NODE_MIDDLE } from './figures'
+
+interface TimelineRow {
+  cells: [name: string, locator: string, start: string, duration: string, location: string]
+  status?: 'pass' | 'fail'
+}
+
+const MAX_STEPS = 10
+
+export function formatTraceTimeline(artifacts: TestArtifact[], root: string): string | undefined {
+  const attempt = [...getTraceAttemptMap(artifacts).values()].at(-1)
+  if (!attempt) {
+    return
+  }
+
+  // the test end is already shown by the error location
+  const visible = attempt.entries.filter((step) => step.name !== 'vitest:onAfterRetryTask')
+  if (!visible.length) {
+    return
+  }
+  const shown = visible.slice(-MAX_STEPS)
+  const prefixes = getTreePrefixes(shown)
+  const headerRow: TimelineRow = { cells: ['step', 'locator', 'start', 'duration', 'location'] }
+  const rows = [headerRow, ...shown.map((step, i) => formatStep(step, prefixes[i], root))]
+
+  const widths = headerRow.cells.map((_, i) => Math.max(...rows.map((row) => row.cells[i].length)))
+  const lines = rows.map((row) => {
+    // the last column is left unpadded so rows have no trailing spaces inside its color codes
+    const [name, locator, start, duration, location] = row.cells.map((cell, i) =>
+      i === 4 ? cell : i === 2 || i === 3 ? cell.padStart(widths[i]) : cell.padEnd(widths[i]),
+    )
+    if (row === headerRow) {
+      return c.dim(`  ${name}  ${locator}  ${start}  ${duration}  ${location}`)
+    }
+    const text = `  ${name}  ${colorCell(locator, c.cyan)}  ${start}  ${colorCell(duration)}  ${colorCell(location, c.dim)}`
+    return row.status === 'fail' ? c.red(text) : text
+  })
+  const omitted = visible.length - shown.length
+  if (omitted) {
+    lines.splice(1, 0, c.dim(`  ... ${omitted} earlier ${omitted === 1 ? 'step' : 'steps'}`))
+  }
+
+  const header: string[] = []
+  if (attempt.retry) {
+    header.push(`retry ${attempt.retry}`)
+  }
+  if (attempt.repeats) {
+    header.push(`repeat ${attempt.repeats}`)
+  }
+  const title = header.length ? `Trace (${header.join(', ')}):` : 'Trace:'
+  return [`\n${title}`, ...lines].join('\n')
+}
+
+function getTreePrefixes(steps: NormalizedBrowserTraceEntry[]): string[] {
+  const hasNextSibling = steps.map((step, i) => {
+    const next = steps.slice(i + 1).find((other) => other.depth <= step.depth)
+    return next?.depth === step.depth
+  })
+  const lastAtDepth: number[] = []
+  return steps.map((step, i) => {
+    lastAtDepth[step.depth] = i
+    if (step.depth === 0) {
+      return ''
+    }
+    let prefix = ''
+    for (let level = 1; level < step.depth; level++) {
+      prefix += hasNextSibling[lastAtDepth[level]] ? '│   ' : '    '
+    }
+    return `${prefix}${hasNextSibling[i] ? F_TREE_NODE_MIDDLE : F_TREE_NODE_END} `
+  })
+}
+
+function formatStep(step: NormalizedBrowserTraceEntry, prefix: string, root: string): TimelineRow {
+  const location =
+    step.location &&
+    `${relative(root, step.location.file)}:${step.location.line}:${step.location.column}`
+  return {
+    cells: [
+      `${prefix}${formatStepName(step.name)}`,
+      step.element?.locator || '-',
+      `+${formatMs(step.startTime)}`,
+      step.duration == null ? '-' : formatMs(step.duration),
+      location || '-',
+    ],
+    status: step.status,
+  }
+}
+
+function colorCell(cell: string, format = (text: string) => text): string {
+  return cell.trim() === '-' ? c.dim(cell) : format(cell)
+}
+
+function formatMs(ms: number): string {
+  return `${Math.round(ms)}ms`
+}
+
+function formatStepName(name: string): string {
+  return name.startsWith('vitest:') ? name.slice('vitest:'.length) : name
+}
+
+// TODO: everything below is copied from `BrowserTraceData`/`BrowserTraceEntry` in
+// packages/browser/src/client/tester/trace.ts (only the fields used here) and
+// `getTraceAttemptMap` in packages/ui/client/composables/trace-view.ts.
+// share them instead (https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11604)
+
+interface BrowserTraceData {
+  retry: number
+  repeats: number
+  entries: BrowserTraceEntry[]
+}
+
+interface BrowserTraceEntry {
+  name: string
+  range?: { id: string; phase: 'start' | 'end' }
+  status?: 'pass' | 'fail'
+  startTime: number
+  duration?: number
+  location?: { file: string; line: number; column: number }
+  element?: { locator: string }
+}
+
+interface NormalizedBrowserTraceData extends BrowserTraceData {
+  entries: NormalizedBrowserTraceEntry[]
+}
+
+interface NormalizedBrowserTraceEntry extends BrowserTraceEntry {
+  depth: number
+}
+
+function getTraceAttemptKey(trace: BrowserTraceData): string {
+  return `${trace.repeats}:${trace.retry}`
+}
+
+function normalizeTraceEntries(entries: BrowserTraceEntry[]): NormalizedBrowserTraceEntry[] {
+  const merged: NormalizedBrowserTraceEntry[] = []
+  const startMap = new Map<string, number>()
+  const parents: string[] = []
+
+  for (const entry of entries) {
+    const range = entry.range
+    if (!range) {
+      merged.push({
+        ...entry,
+        depth: parents.length,
+      })
+      continue
+    }
+
+    if (range.phase === 'start') {
+      startMap.set(range.id, merged.length)
+      merged.push({
+        ...entry,
+        depth: parents.length,
+      })
+      parents.push(range.id)
+      continue
+    }
+
+    // when range.phase === 'end'
+    const index = startMap.get(range.id)
+    if (index == null) {
+      // unpaired range shouldn't happen but just leave it there
+      merged.push({ ...entry, depth: 0 })
+      continue
+    }
+
+    // Keep the start timestamp for positioning, but derive display duration
+    // from the end event timestamp.
+    const start = merged[index]
+    merged[index] = {
+      ...start,
+      ...entry,
+      startTime: start.startTime,
+      duration: entry.startTime - start.startTime,
+    }
+    parents.pop()
+  }
+
+  return merged
+}
+
+function getTraceAttemptMap(artifacts: TestArtifact[]): Map<string, NormalizedBrowserTraceData> {
+  const grouped: Record<string, BrowserTraceData[]> = {}
+  for (const artifact of artifacts) {
+    if (artifact.type !== 'internal:browserTrace') {
+      continue
+    }
+    const trace = artifact.data as BrowserTraceData
+    const key = getTraceAttemptKey(trace)
+    grouped[key] ??= []
+    grouped[key].push(trace)
+  }
+
+  const merged = new Map<string, NormalizedBrowserTraceData>()
+  for (const [key, traces] of Object.entries(grouped)) {
+    const trace = traces[0]
+    const entries = traces.flatMap((trace) => trace.entries)
+    merged.set(key, {
+      ...trace,
+      entries: normalizeTraceEntries(entries),
+    })
+  }
+  return merged
+}

+import type { TestFsStructure } from '../../test-utils'
+import { expect, test } from 'vitest'
+import { instances, runInlineBrowserTests } from './utils'
+
+async function runBrowserTests(structure: TestFsStructure) {
+  return runInlineBrowserTests(structure, {
+    reporters: 'default',
+    browser: {
+      ui: false,
+      instances: instances.slice(0, 1),
+      traceView: true,
+      screenshotFailures: false,
+    },
+  })
+}
+
+function extractTimelines(stderr: string) {
+  return [...stderr.matchAll(/\nTrace\b.*?\n\n/gs)].map((match) => {
+    const [title, ...lines] = match[0].trim().split('\n')
+    const rows = lines.map((line) =>
+      line
+        .trim()
+        .replace(/\d+(\.\d+)?m?s\b/g, '<time>')
+        // columns can differ between browsers
+        .replace(/(\.test\.ts:\d+):\d+/g, '$1')
+        .split(/ {2,}/),
+    )
+    const widths = rows[0].map((_, i) => Math.max(...rows.map((row) => row[i]?.length ?? 0)))
+    const table = rows.map((row) =>
+      row
+        .map((cell, i) => cell.padEnd(widths[i]))
+        .join('  ')
+        .trimEnd(),
+    )
+    return [title, ...table].join('\n')
+  })
+}
+
+test('prints trace timeline on failure', async () => {
+  const { stderr } = await runBrowserTests({
+    'basic.test.ts': /* ts */ `
+      import { expect, test } from 'vitest'
+      import { page } from 'vitest/browser'
+
+      test('pass', async () => {
+        document.body.innerHTML = '<button>Load</button>'
+        await page.getByRole('button').click()
+      })
+
+      test('fail', async () => {
+        document.body.innerHTML = '<button>Load</button>'
+        await page.mark('load', async () => {
+          await page.getByRole('button').click()
+          await expect.element(page.getByRole('button')).toHaveTextContent('Load')
+        })
+        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 300))
+        await page.mark('after wait')
+        await expect.element(page.getByRole('button'), { timeout: 100 }).toHaveTextContent('Done')
+      })
+    `,
+  })
+
+  expect(extractTimelines(stderr)).toMatchInlineSnapshot(`
+    [
+      "Trace:
+    step                       locator              start    duration  location
+    load                       -                    +<time>  <time>    basic.test.ts:12
+    ├── click                  getByRole('button')  +<time>  <time>    basic.test.ts:13
+    └── toHaveTextContent      getByRole('button')  +<time>  <time>    basic.test.ts:14
+    after wait                 -                    +<time>  -         basic.test.ts:17
+    toHaveTextContent [ERROR]  getByRole('button')  +<time>  <time>    basic.test.ts:18",
+    ]
+  `)
+})
+
+test('prints trace timeline for a failure outside trace steps', async () => {
+  const { stderr } = await runBrowserTests({

bug.description: The retryer always schedules a pause after the delay when canContinue is false, even if the retry has already been resolved or cancelled. This allows a cancelled retry to pause a replacement fetch, overwriting its status.

bug.description: The code uses `query?.state.error` to decide whether to evaluate a function-valued `throwOnError`. If the query error is falsy (e.g., undefined), the function is never called and its return value is ignored, causing `throwOnError` to be treated as truthy and disabling `retryOnMount`. This logic fails for falsy errors.

+## Mutation Scopes
+
+Per default, all mutations run in parallel - even if you invoke `.mutate()` of the same mutation multiple times. Mutations can be given a `scope` with an `id` to avoid that. @@ -0,0 +1,135 @@
+import type { Context } from '../../context.ts'
+import type { MiddlewareHandler } from '../../types.ts'
+import '../../context.ts'
+
+declare module '../../context.ts' {
+  interface ContextVariableMap {
+    metric?: {
+      headers: string[]
+      timers: Map<string, Timer>
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+interface Timer {
+  description?: string
+  start: number
+}
+
+interface TimingOptions {
+  total: boolean
+  enabled: boolean | ((c: Context) => boolean)
+  totalDescription: string
+  autoEnd: boolean
+  crossOrigin: boolean | string
+}
+
+const getTime = () => {
+  try {
+    return performance.now()
+  } catch {}
+  return Date.now()
+}
+
+export const timing = (config?: Partial<TimingOptions>): MiddlewareHandler => {
+  const options: TimingOptions = {
+    ...{
+      total: true,
+      enabled: true,
+      totalDescription: 'Total Response Time',
+      autoEnd: true,
+      crossOrigin: false,
+    },
+    ...config,
+  }
+  return async (c, next) => {
+    const headers: string[] = []
+    const timers = new Map<string, Timer>()
+    c.set('metric', { headers, timers })
+
+    if (options.total) {
+      startTime(c, 'total', options.totalDescription)
+    }
+    await next()
+
+    if (options.total) {
+      endTime(c, 'total')
+    }
+
+    if (options.autoEnd) {
+      timers.forEach((_, key) => endTime(c, key))
+    }
+
+    const enabled = typeof options.enabled === 'function' ? options.enabled(c) : options.enabled
+
+    if (enabled) {
+      c.res.headers.append('Server-Timing', headers.join(','))
+      if (options.crossOrigin) {
+        c.res.headers.append(
+          'Timing-Allow-Origin',
+          typeof options.crossOrigin === 'string' ? options.crossOrigin : '*'
+        )
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+interface SetMetric {
+  (c: Context, name: string, value: number, description?: string, precision?: number): void
+
+  (c: Context, name: string, description?: string): void
+}
+
+export const setMetric: SetMetric = (
+  c: Context,
+  name: string,
+  valueDescription: number | string | undefined,
+  description?: string,
+  precision?: number
+) => {
+  const metrics = c.get('metric')
+  if (!metrics) {
+    console.warn('Metrics not initialized! Please add the `timing()` middleware to this route!')
+    return
+  }
+  if (typeof valueDescription === 'number') {
+    const dur = valueDescription.toFixed(precision || 1)
+
+    const metric = description ? `${name};dur=${dur};desc="${description}"` : `${name};dur=${dur}`
+
+    metrics.headers.push(metric)
+  } else {
+    // Value-less metric
+    const metric = valueDescription ? `${name};desc="${valueDescription}"` : `${name}`
+
+    metrics.headers.push(metric)
+  }
+}
+
+export const startTime = (c: Context, name: string, description?: string) => {
+  const metrics = c.get('metric')
+  if (!metrics) {
+    console.warn('Metrics not initialized! Please add the `timing()` middleware to this route!')
+    return
+  }
+  metrics.timers.set(name, { description, start: getTime() })
+}
+
+export const endTime = (c: Context, name: string, precision?: number) => {
+  const metrics = c.get('metric')
+  if (!metrics) {
+    console.warn('Metrics not initialized! Please add the `timing()` middleware to this route!')
+    return
+  }
+  const timer = metrics.timers.get(name)
+  if (!timer) {
+    console.warn(`Timer "${name}" does not exist!`)
+    return
+  }
+  const { description, start } = timer
+
+  const duration = getTime() - start
+
+  setMetric(c, name, duration, description, precision)

+import type { Context } from '../../context'
+import type { MiddlewareHandler } from '../../types'
+import '../../context'
+
+declare module '../../context' {
+  interface ContextVariableMap {
+    metric?: {
+      headers: string[]
+      timers: Map<string, Timer>
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+interface Timer {
+  description?: string
+  start: number
+}
+
+interface TimingOptions {
+  total: boolean
+  enabled: boolean | ((c: Context) => boolean)
+  totalDescription: string
+  autoEnd: boolean
+  crossOrigin: boolean | string
+}
+
+const getTime = () => {
+  try {
+    return performance.now()
+  } catch {}
+  return Date.now()
+}
+
+export const timing = (config?: Partial<TimingOptions>): MiddlewareHandler => {
+  const options: TimingOptions = {
+    ...{
+      total: true,
+      enabled: true,
+      totalDescription: 'Total Response Time',
+      autoEnd: true,
+      crossOrigin: false,
+    },
+    ...config,
+  }
+  return async (c, next) => {
+    const headers: string[] = []
+    const timers = new Map<string, Timer>()
+    c.set('metric', { headers, timers })
+
+    if (options.total) {
+      startTime(c, 'total', options.totalDescription)
+    }
+    await next()
+
+    if (options.total) {
+      endTime(c, 'total')
+    }
+
+    if (options.autoEnd) {
+      timers.forEach((_, key) => endTime(c, key))
+    }
+
+    const enabled = typeof options.enabled === 'function' ? options.enabled(c) : options.enabled
+
+    if (enabled) {
+      c.res.headers.append('Server-Timing', headers.join(','))
+      if (options.crossOrigin) {
+        c.res.headers.append(
+          'Timing-Allow-Origin',
+          typeof options.crossOrigin === 'string' ? options.crossOrigin : '*'
+        )
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+interface SetMetric {
+  (c: Context, name: string, value: number, description?: string, precision?: number): void
+
+  (c: Context, name: string, description?: string): void
+}
+
+export const setMetric: SetMetric = (
+  c: Context,
+  name: string,
+  valueDescription: number | string | undefined,
+  description?: string,
+  precision?: number
+) => {
+  const metrics = c.get('metric')
+  if (!metrics) {
+    console.warn('Metrics not initialized! Please add the `timing()` middleware to this route!')
+    return
+  }
+  if (typeof valueDescription === 'number') {
+    const dur = valueDescription.toFixed(precision || 1)
+
+    const metric = description ? `${name};dur=${dur};desc="${description}"` : `${name};dur=${dur}`
+
+    metrics.headers.push(metric)
+  } else {
+    // Value-less metric
+    const metric = valueDescription ? `${name};desc="${valueDescription}"` : `${name}`
+
+    metrics.headers.push(metric)
+  }
+}
+
+export const startTime = (c: Context, name: string, description?: string) => {
+  const metrics = c.get('metric')
+  if (!metrics) {
+    console.warn('Metrics not initialized! Please add the `timing()` middleware to this route!')
+    return
+  }
+  metrics.timers.set(name, { description, start: getTime() })
+}
+
+export const endTime = (c: Context, name: string, precision?: number) => {
+  const metrics = c.get('metric')
+  if (!metrics) {
+    console.warn('Metrics not initialized! Please add the `timing()` middleware to this route!')
+    return
+  }
+  const timer = metrics.timers.get(name)
+  if (!timer) {
+    console.warn(`Timer "${name}" does not exist!`)
+    return
+  }
+  const { description, start } = timer
+
+  const duration = getTime() - start
+
+  setMetric(c, name, duration, description, precision)
+  metrics.timers.delete(name)
+}

pr.title: fix(context): don't throw the error with `c.header()` when it's finalized (#4078)

bug.description: The added check resets the response with a new Response whenever `this.finalized` is true, discarding the existing response body and headers, which causes errors when `c.header()` is called after the response has been finalized.

fixPr.title: fix(context): allow `c.header()` after the response body is consumed (#5587)

pr.title: feat(csrf): Support async `IsAllowedSecFetchSiteHandler` (#4559)
fix(v4): stop the memoizer copying every issue below each recursive node (#6705)

bug.description: The memoizer recorded issues for each node without accounting for the start index of newly added issues, causing encode passes that skip checks to reuse issue lists from earlier unchecked passes, leading to incorrect validation of nested recursive structures.

fixPr.title: fix(v4): run nested checks when encoding a recursive schema (#6707)

pr.title: fix(v4): keep a memoized node's cached issues private to the cache (#6443)

bug.description: The memoizer clones the full list of issues for every cache hit, copying issue objects (including their paths) each time a node is revisited, which causes memory usage to grow dramatically with recursion depth, leading to crashes.

fixPr.title: fix(v4): stop the memoizer copying every issue below each recursive node (#6705)

pr.title: fix(v4): check array, set and map size bounds before parsing elements (#6652)

bug.description: The early size‑bound check is gated by `!ctx?.skipChecks && ctx?.direction !== "backward"`, which prevents the bound from being applied when a preceding refinement or custom check is present or during encode, allowing oversized arrays/sets/maps to be parsed element‑by‑element instead of failing early.

fixPr.title: fix(v4): check a size bound placed after a refinement, and on encode (#6698)

pr.title: fix: consistently strip __proto__ from parsed objects (#6386)

bug.description: The PR adds a blanket `if (key === "__proto__") continue;` before running the record’s key schema, which skips validation of __proto__ keys entirely. As a result, a key that should be rejected by the key schema is silently accepted and never validated.

fixPr.title: fix(v4): run a record's key schema on an own __proto__ key (#6660)

pr.title: fix: remove exponential backtracking from the emoji regex (#6347)

bug.description: The `_emoji` regex was defined as `^[\p{Extended_Pictographic}\p{Emoji_Component}]+$`, which also matches strings consisting only of Emoji_Component characters (e.g., digits, "#", "*", variation selectors) that are not valid emojis, leading to false‑positive validation.

fixPr.title: fix(v4): reject component-only strings from z.emoji() (#6532)

pr.title: fix(v4): complete reserved-key hardening (#6371)

bug.description: The added code always adds the keys to the JSON Schema "required" list even when the record's value schema can fill missing keys (e.g., default/optional), because it fails to consider the value’s optional‑in marker, leading to required keys that should be omitted on input.

fixPr.title: fix(v4): make record input keys optional when the value can fill them (#6460)

pr.title: fix: correct multipleOf float validation using tolerance-based comparison (#5793)

bug.description: The introduced floatSafeRemainder uses a tolerance of Number.EPSILON * max(|ratio|,1), which is too strict for decimal multiples; it incorrectly rejects values that are exact multiples due to floating‑point rounding errors.

fixPr.title: fix(v4): accept exact decimal multiples in multipleOf (#6223)

pr.title: Add includes position regex (#4602)

bug.description: The new includes check builds a regex using `^.{${def.position}}${escapedRegex}`, which forces the substring to appear exactly at the given offset, but `String.prototype.includes(sub, position)` should match at that offset or any later position. This off‑by‑one semantics error causes mismatched validation and JSON schema output.

fixPr.title: fix(v4): let the includes(position) pattern match at or after the offset (#6024)

pr.title: feat: add hr translation (#5610)
feat: add map support to Uzbek locale (#5599)
fix(adapter): fix progress event emitting; (#6518)

bug.description: The original code calls `flushUpload` and `flushDownload` in the `done` handler without removing the associated event listeners, potentially leaving dangling listeners and causing memory leaks or unintended callbacks after the request completes.

fixPr.title: fix(xhr): remove progress event listeners on request completion (#11225)

pr.title: refactor(http): extract Http2Sessions into its own module (#10861)

bug.description: The original code removed a session from the pool only when all streams closed, but it never handled the HTTP/2 GOAWAY event. As a result, a session that received GOAWAY could still be reused and an idle timer could be scheduled for a session that was already removed, potentially delaying process exit.

fixPr.title: fix(http2): stop reusing sessions after GOAWAY (#11210)

pr.title: fix(http): preserve TLS options for proxy tunnels (#10957)

bug.description: The diff adds logic to merge the user-supplied httpsAgent options into the tunneling agent’s callback, but it ignores the case where no httpsAgent is provided and the global https.globalAgent should supply TLS options for the origin connection. This omission causes the origin TLS upgrade to miss custom global TLS settings such as a custom CA.

fixPr.title: fix(http): apply https.globalAgent TLS options to proxy tunnels (#11178)

pr.title: fix(interceptors): trim trailing ejected handlers (#11087)

bug.description: The interceptor manager stores handlers in a Map keyed by numeric IDs, but the eject method still accepts string IDs and looks them up directly in the Map, causing string IDs to fail to remove handlers.

fixPr.title: fix(interceptors): restore numeric-string interceptor IDs (#11139)

pr.title: fix(fromDataURI): accept case-insensitive base64 tokens (#11138)

bug.description: The change to accept case‑insensitive base64 markers caused the buffer‑allocation estimate to use the raw body length, which inflates the size for percent‑encoded base64 data and allows oversized inputs to pass the limit.

fixPr.title: fix(http): decode percent-encoded Base64 data URLs (#11294)

pr.title: fix: unrestricted cloud metadata exfiltration via header injection chain (#10660)

bug.description: The original code attempted to avoid duplicating stack traces by comparing the end of the existing stack to a suffix that omitted the first two frames of the newly captured stack. This logic incorrectly suppressed appending the full reconstructed stack when the suffix was empty or when the existing stack already ended with that suffix, leading to missing caller context in error stacks.

fixPr.title: fix(core): preserve short reconstructed request stacks (#11132)

pr.title: fix: fetch adaptor is not enforcing max body or content length (#10795)

bug.description: The fetch adapter throws an AxiosError when the response body exceeds maxContentLength, but that error is not preserved when the runtime (e.g., browsers or undici) wraps the fetch rejection, causing the original error’s request and config context to be lost.

fixPr.title: fix(fetch): preserve response size errors across runtime wrappers (#11179)

pr.title: fix: added fix for memory leak in sockets (#10788)

bug.description: The original code added an error listener that closed over the outer `socket` variable, causing the listener to retain a reference to the request that first used the socket and preventing the socket from being garbage‑collected. A reviewer could spot that the listener should use the socket’s current request via the symbol, not the outer variable.

fixPr.title: fix(http): stop per-socket error listener from retaining the installing request's context (memory leak) (#11091)

pr.title: feat: compatibility with frozen prototypes (#6265)
perf(http): fix early loop exit; (#7202)

+import addMinutes from '../addMinutes/index'
+import toDate from '../toDate/index'
+import startOfMinute from '../startOfMinute/index'
+import requiredArgs from '../_lib/requiredArgs/index'
+
+import { Interval, StepOptions } from '../types'
+
+/**
+ * @name eachMinuteOfInterval
+ * @category Interval Helpers
+ * @summary Return the array of minutes within the specified time interval.
+ *
+ * @description
+ * Returns the array of minutes within the specified time interval.
+ *
+ * @param {Interval} interval - the interval. See [Interval]{@link https://date-fns.org/docs/Interval}
+ * @param {Object} [options] - an object with options.
+ * @param {Number} [options.step=1] - the step to increment by. The starts of minutes from the hour of the interval start to the hour of the interval end
+ * @throws {TypeError} 1 argument requie value should be more than 1.
+ * @returns {Date[]} the array withred
+ * @throws {RangeError} `options.step` must be a number equal or greater than 1
+ * @throws {RangeError} The start of an interval cannot be after its end
+ * @throws {RangeError} Date in interval cannot be `Invalid Date`
+ *
+ * @example
+ * // Each minute between 14 October 2020, 13:00 and 14 October 2020, 13:03
+ * const result = eachMinuteOfInterval({
+ *   start: new Date(2014, 9, 14, 13),
+ *   end: new Date(2014, 9, 14, 13, 3)
+ * })
+ * //=> [
+ * //   Wed Oct 14 2014 13:00:00,
+ * //   Wed Oct 14 2014 13:01:00,
+ * //   Wed Oct 14 2014 13:02:00,
+ * //   Wed Oct 14 2014 13:03:00
+ * // ]
+ */
+export default function eachMinuteOfInterval(
+  interval: Interval,
+  options?: StepOptions
+): Date[] {
+  requiredArgs(1, arguments)
+
+  const startDate = startOfMinute(toDate(interval.start))
+  const endDate = startOfMinute(toDate(interval.end))
+
+  const startTime = startDate.getTime()
+  const endTime = endDate.getTime()
+
+  if (startTime >= endTime) {
+    throw new RangeError('Invalid interval')
+  }
+
+  const dates = []
+
+  let currentDate = startDate
+
+  const step = options && 'step' in options ? Number(options.step) : 1
+  if (step < 1 || isNaN(step))
+    throw new RangeError(
+      '`options.step` must be a number equal or greater than 1'
+    )
+
+  while (currentDate.getTime() <= endTime) {
+    dates.push(toDate(currentDate))
+    currentDate = addMinutes(currentDate, step)
+  }
+
+  return dates
+}

+// @flow

+
+import assert from 'power-assert'
+
+import eachMinuteOfInterval from '.'
+

+  it('should return an array of Date objects containing a Date for each minute between the interval', () => {
+    const result = eachMinuteOfInterval({
+      start: new Date(2020, 10, 14, 13, 0),
+      end: new Date(2020, 10, 14, 13, 5)
+    })
+
+    assert.deepEqual(result, [
+      new Date(2020, 10, 14, 13, 0),
+      new Date(2020, 10, 14, 13, 1),
+      new Date(2020, 10, 14, 13, 2),
+      new Date(2020, 10, 14, 13, 3),
+      new Date(2020, 10, 14, 13, 4),
+      new Date(2020, 10, 14, 13, 5)
+    ])
+  })
+

+    const result = eachMinuteOfInterval({

+      end: new Date(2020, 10, 14, 13, 2)

+
+    assert.deepEqual(result[0], new Date(2020, 10, 14, 13))
+    assert.deepEqual(result[2], new Date(2020, 10, 14, 13, 2))
+  })
+
+  it('should accept timestamps', () => {
+    const start = new Date(2020, 10, 14, 13, 0).getTime()
+    const end = new Date(2020, 10, 14, 13, 2).getTime()
+
+    const result = eachMinuteOfInterval({
+      start,
+      end
+    })
+
+    assert.deepEqual(result, [

+    })

+  })
+
+  describe('options.step', () => {

+    }
+
+    const stepError = /^RangeError: `options.step` must be a number equal or greater than 1$/
+
+    it('returns an array with starts of hours from the hour of the start date to the hour of the end date with the given step', () => {
+      const result = eachMinuteOfInterval(interval, { step: 3 })
+      assert.deepEqual(result, [
+        new Date(2020, 9, 14, 13, 1),
+        new Date(2020, 9, 14, 13, 4),
+        new Date(2020, 9, 14, 13, 7)
+      ])
+    })
+
+    it('throws TypeError error if `options.step` is less than 1', () => {
+      assert.throws(
+        () => eachMinuteOfInterval(interval, { step: 0 }),
+        stepError
+      )
+      assert.throws(
+        () => eachMinuteOfInterval(interval, { step: -3 }),

+    it('throws TypeError error if `options.step` is NaN', () => {

+      )

+        stepError
+      )

 ## `formatRelative`

bug.description: The code returns the string 'o chionn' concatenated directly with the result, missing a space before the result, producing malformed output such as 'o chionn1 mionaid' instead of 'o chionn 1 mionaid'.

fixPr.title: Fix Scottish Gaelic (gd) locale  (#1925)

bug.fixDiff:
diff --git a/src/locale/gd/_lib/formatDistance/index.js b/src/locale/gd/_lib/formatDistance/index.js

@@ -107,7 +107,7 @@ export default function formatDistance(token, count, options) {
     if (options.comparison > 0) {
       return 'ann an ' + result
     } else {
-      return ' o chionn' + result
+      return 'o chionn ' + result
     }
   }

bug.description: The introduced month parsing regexes use /^1/, /^2/, etc., which match any string starting with those digits—including standalone digits that should not be interpreted as months—leading to incorrect month parsing in Japanese locale.

bug.description: The original code added the timezone offset twice by calling getTimezoneOffsetInMilliseconds on the same timestamp, causing incorrect handling of daylight‑saving transitions.

fixPr.title: Fix DST issue (closes #972, closes #992) (#1003)

bug.fixDiff:
diff --git a/src/toDate/index.js b/src/toDate/index.js
index 06a443e8e..0151f3a09 100644
--- a/src/toDate/index.js
+++ b/src/toDate/index.js
@@ -186,11 +186,20 @@ export default function toDate(argument, dirtyOptions) {
         return new Date(NaN)
       }
     } else {
-      // get offset accurate to hour in timezones that change offset
-      offset = getTimezoneOffsetInMilliseconds(new Date(timestamp + time))
-      offset = getTimezoneOffsetInMilliseconds(
-        new Date(timestamp + time + offset)
-      )
+      var fullTime = timestamp + time
+      var fullTimeDate = new Date(fullTime)
+
+      offset = getTimezoneOffsetInMilliseconds(fullTimeDate)
+
+      // Adjust time when it's coming from DST
+      var fullTimeDateNextDay = new Date(fullTime)
+      fullTimeDateNextDay.setDate(fullTimeDate.getDate() + 1)
+      var offsetDiff =
+        getTimezoneOffsetInMilliseconds(fullTimeDateNextDay) -
+        getTimezoneOffsetInMilliseconds(fullTimeDate)
+      if (offsetDiff > 0) {
+        offset += offsetDiff
+      }
     }
 
     return new Date(timestamp + time + offset)

bug.description: The earlier PR added a guard that skips drafting a value if the array index is present in `assigned_`. After array mutations like push, unshift, splice, or index writes, `assigned_` is keyed by index and no longer reflects the actual value at that position, so a relocated base object can be returned undrafted and mutate the base state.

fixPr.title: fix: draft relocated base objects at previously assigned indices in array-methods plugin (#1314)

pr.title: fix: #768 `immerable` field being lost during patch value cloning (#771)

bug.description: The patch application logic incorrectly slices the patch list only when producing a new copy of the base state, but not when applying patches directly to a draft. This causes patches that should be applied after a full-state replacement to be dropped, leading to incorrect state updates.

fixPr.title: fix: Append to array when key is "-" (#872)

pr.title: feat: Optimize Immer performance where possible, introduce `setUseStrictIteration` (#1164)
Improve progress events for `onDownloadProgress` and `onUploadProgress` (#736)

bug.description: The progress stream’s flush handler only emits a final progress event when a previous chunk exists, so an empty request or response body never triggers a progress callback, breaking the API contract for empty transfers.

fixPr.title: Fix progress callbacks for empty request and response bodies (#881)

pr.title: Fix `signal` merging when using both instance and request options (#751)

bug.description: The original merge logic treated any AbortSignal value as a signal to merge, even when the signal was provided at the root options level and should have replaced or cleared existing signals. This caused signals from instance defaults and request options to be combined incorrectly, leading to unexpected abort behavior.

fixPr.title: Fix `signal` replacement when extending instances (#880)

pr.title: Add `retry.jitter` option (#760)

bug.description: The code uses Math.min(this.#options.retry.backoffLimit, jitteredDelay) without handling the case where backoffLimit is undefined, causing Math.min(undefined, …) to return NaN and break retry delay calculation.

fixPr.title: Fix: Handle `backoffLimit` being `undefined` (#796)

pr.title: Fix multipart boundary mismatch (#540)

bug.description: The change incorrectly excludes any option that exists on the Request object from being forwarded to fetch, even when the option is vendor‑specific and should still be passed (e.g., Next.js’s `next` option). This logic error causes valid options to be dropped.

fixPr.title: Fix Next.js edge runtime `next` option support (#775)

pr.title: Fetch with an uncloned request when possible (#601)

bug.description: The code clones the request for retries but then passes the original request to the fetch/timeout logic, while cleanup only cancels the cloned request’s body. This leaves the original request’s body unused and uncanceled, causing a memory leak.

fixPr.title: Fix hang on stream request cleanup in Node.js (#741)

pr.title: Fix the empty check for `.json()` (#466)

bug.description: The diff reads the response body twice: first by cloning and calling `arrayBuffer()` to check size, then later by calling `response.text()`. This double consumption of the body causes a runtime error because the body can only be read once, leading to a race condition.

fixPr.title: Fix race condition issue with `.json()` (#731)

pr.title: Add onUploadProgress option (#632)

bug.description: The code passes the request to `streamRequest` after the body has already been transformed into a stream, so `streamRequest` calculates the total upload size from the already‑streamed body, yielding an incorrect size and causing the upload progress callback to report wrong values.

fixPr.title: Fix `uploadProgress` with form data (#725)

pr.title: Fix support with environments that add support for custom `fetch` options (#536)

bug.description: The original code only checked whether an option key existed on the Request object or in the kyOptionKeys set, so any valid RequestInit properties (e.g., `method`, `headers`, `body`) were incorrectly flagged as unknown options, causing runtime errors when those options were passed.

fixPr.title: Fix multipart boundary mismatch (#540)

pr.title: feat(serveStatic): support default and custom mimes (#1137)

bug.description: The getType function uses the file extension as a key in the MIME type map without normalizing case, causing MIME resolution to fail for uppercase or mixed‑case extensions.

fixPr.title: fix(static): match file extensions case-insensitively (#1580)

pr.title: feat!: `HTTPResponse` (#1212)

bug.description: The `noContent` and `redirect` helpers hard‑coded statusText values for specific status codes (204, 301, 302) instead of using the standard reason phrase for the given status. This caused incorrect or missing statusText for other status codes, e.g., `noContent(200)` returned an empty body with statusText "No Content" and `redirect` with status 300 returned "Moved Permanently".

fixPr.title: fix(response): use matching reason phrases in redirect and noContent (#1570)

pr.title: feat: typed `event.req` and experimental `defineValidatedHandler` (#1097)

bug.description: The handler’s query parsing logic discarded repeated query parameters, converting them to a single string value instead of preserving all values as an array.

fixPr.title: fix(validate): preserve repeated query values in defineValidatedHandler (#1562)

pr.title: feat: platform agnostic `serveStatic` utility (#480)

bug.description: The original code only set the Vary header when more than one encoding was accepted, ignoring cases where a single encoding (or identity) was requested, leading to incorrect caching behavior.

fixPr.title: fix(static): set vary header when a single encoding is accepted (#1556)

pr.title: refactor(sse): promote EventStream to public API, deprecate createEventStream (#1509)

bug.description: The refactor added an onDispose handler that calls `close()` (or cancels the readable) without accounting for the possibility that a flush is already in progress or that data is buffered while the stream is paused. This can lead to overlapping flushes or close operations that duplicate or lose buffered events, causing incorrect event delivery.

fixPr.title: fix(sse): preserve buffered events during overlapping flushes (#1555)

pr.title: feat: session support (#315)

bug.description: The original `getSession` implementation immediately persisted a newly created session by calling `updateSession`, causing a `Set-Cookie` header to be sent even when the session was only read. This eager persistence was unintended and broke the contract that reading a session should not start one.

fixPr.title: fix(session): do not persist a session that is only read (#1541)

pr.title: fix(iterable): always encode chunks (#847)

bug.description: The hand‑rolled base64 encoder builds an array of character codes and then calls `String.fromCharCode(...bytes)`. For large payloads this spreads more arguments than the JavaScript engine allows, causing a runtime crash. The bug is in the fallback branch that is used when `Buffer` is not available.

fixPr.title: fix(session): encode large payloads outside node-compatible runtimes (#1515)

pr.title: refactor: improve response and hooks handling (#1008)

bug.description: The original code called `prepareResponse` directly and then wrapped the result in a promise chain. If `prepareResponse` threw synchronously (e.g., due to a circular JSON value or a thrown error), that exception would escape the async flow and bypass the error handling pipeline, causing the request to fail with an unhandled exception instead of a normal 500 response.

fixPr.title: fix(response): route synchronous prepareResponse throws through the error pipeline (#1503)

pr.title: feat(defineWebSocketHandler): support callback with `event`  (#1242)
feat: `toMiddleware` util (#1234)
